  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X
}
\toprule
\textbf{TCM (energetic anatomy)} & \textbf{$\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism} \\
\midrule
12 principal meridians & 12 base pentads ($P_1$ to $P_6$, $N_1$ to $N_6$) \\
\addlinespace
Circulation of \textit{qi} in the meridians & Circulation of configurations between attractors \\
\addlinespace
Acupuncture points (穴位) on the meridians & Polar thresholds $P_4$ and $N_4$ (hinges between belts) \\
\addlinespace
Imbalance of the meridians & Topological frustration ($E_{k,g} > 0$) \\
\addlinespace
Homeostasis & Nilpotency $(g \cdot x)^2 = 0$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

**Status of this correspondence.** The table above proposes an **analogy** between the 12 meridians of TCM and the 12 pentads of $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$. This analogy is **heuristic**: it helps to understand why the model can be read as an "energetic anatomy" of the economy (circulation, critical points, imbalances, homeostasis). It does **not** constitute a demonstration of isomorphism. To speak of isomorphism in the strict sense, it would be necessary to:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Model the 12 meridians as a graph} (12 nodes, connection edges, circulation cycles).
\item \textbf{Model the 12 pentads as a graph} (12 nodes, adjacency edges in the Merkabah, Sheng/Ke cycles).
\item \textbf{Show that the two graphs are isomorphic} (same number of nodes, same number of edges, same structure of cycles, same degree distribution).
\item \textbf{Show that the acupuncture points correspond to specific nodes} of the graph (not to the polar thresholds $P_4$ and $N_4$, which are \textbf{pentads}, not points on the meridians).
\end{enumerate}

**What is objectively shared.** The only objective point is the \textbf{number} (12 = 12). The other correspondences are \textbf{functional analogies} (the two "circulate", the two "become imbalanced", the two "rebalance"), not structural isomorphisms.

**Cross-reference.** The operational extension of this analogy (the spectral observables as "four examinations" of TCM) is presented in §15.4.8. The anatomy (§25.3) and the diagnostic practice (§15.4.8) are the two faces of the same **analogy** between TCM and the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism: one describes the \textit{body} of the economic system (its 12 meridians/pentads), the other describes the \textit{method} for taking its pulse (the 4 examinations/observables). This analogy is heuristic, not demonstrative.

This structural correspondence (the 12 meridians ↔ the 12 pentads) finds its operational extension in **§15.4.8**, where the spectral observables are interpreted as the **four examinations** (望闻问切, *wàng wén wèn qiè*) by which the physician takes the pulse of the system. The anatomy (§25.3) and the diagnostic practice (§15.4.8) are thus the two faces of the same isomorphism between TCM and the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism: one describes the *body* of the economic system (its 12 meridians/pentads), the other describes the *method* for taking its pulse (the 4 examinations/observables).

\paragraph{Lesson for the model (heuristic analogy).}

Chinese Stasis can be \textbf{read as} a blockage of economic flows, analogous to an imbalance of the meridians in TCM. This analogy is \textbf{heuristic}: it helps to understand why the TRR acts on \textbf{critical points} (thresholds $P_4$ and $N_4$) rather than on the whole system, and why the three structural reforms target \textbf{specific points} (finance, institutions, territory).

\paragraph{What the analogy does not do.}

It does not \textbf{demonstrate} that the TRR is the only way out, nor that one must activate $P_4$ and $N_4$ rather than another threshold. It \textbf{illustrates} a prescription that rests elsewhere on the spectral diagnosis (Chapter 16) and on the topology of thresholds (Chapter 13). The activation of $P_4$ and $N_4$ is justified by the \textbf{direction of the transition} (exit from Stasis towards expansion), not by the analogy with acupuncture.

\paragraph{Conventional attribution of the reforms to the meridians.}

The identification of the three reforms with specific "meridians" is an \textbf{interpretive convention}:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Two Mountains Bank} $\rightarrow$ finance meridian (reorientation of capital flows towards ecological regeneration);
    \item \textbf{Integration of the GEP into the KPIs} $\rightarrow$ institutions meridian (anchoring of the new productive model);
    \item \textbf{Regenerative Usufruct Certificate (RUC)} $\rightarrow$ territory meridian (creation of a new value-distribution cycle).
\end{itemize}

This attribution is \textbf{suggestive} (it helps to understand the role of each reform), but it is \textbf{not deduced} from the structure of the meridians (which is not formally modelled, cf. §25.3). It could be revised if a more rigorous modelling of the meridians were undertaken.

---

### 25.4. Tang kinship (Wufu) and the regulation of alliances

The Chinese kinship system of the Tang dynasty (618–907, a period considered the apogee of classical China) known as the \textit{Wufu} (五服, "Five Mournings"), is a \textbf{topology of alliances} that defines the degrees of kinship and matrimonial prohibitions. It rests on a structure of 64 matrimonial configurations, filtered into 20 alliance attractors. This structure is analysed in detail in \cite{DeDominicis_2026_Tang_kinship}, where the following are established: (i) the modelling of the 64 configurations as a binary space with 6 traits, (ii) the $64 \to 20$ filtration via the Merkabah neighbourhood rule, (iii) the correspondence between the 20 attractors and the types of alliances observed under the Tang.

**Correspondence with the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism**:

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Analogy between the Wufu kinship system and the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism}
\label{tab:correspondance_wufu_cl66}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.5cm}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X
}
\toprule
\textbf{Wufu} & \textbf{$\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism} \\
\midrule
64 matrimonial configurations & 64 economic configurations \\
\addlinespace
20 alliance attractors & 20 economic attractors \\
\addlinespace
Alliance prohibitions & Frustrated configurations (economic prohibitions) \\
\addlinespace
5 degrees of mourning & Polarity gradient $3P \rightarrow 3N$ (4 levels) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

**Status of this correspondence.** The table above proposes an **analogy** between the Wufu and the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism. This analogy is **heuristic**: it helps to understand why the model can be read as a "topology of alliances" (configurations, attractors, prohibitions). It does **not** constitute a demonstration of isomorphism. To speak of isomorphism in the strict sense, it would be necessary to:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Model the 64 matrimonial configurations of the Wufu} as a space of binary configurations (6 bits) — \textbf{done in \cite{DeDominicis_2026_Tang_kinship}, §1.1.1 and §1.3.2}.
\item \textbf{Model the 20 alliance attractors} as equivalence classes (triplets) — \textbf{done in \cite{DeDominicis_2026_Tang_kinship}, §1.4.2}.
\item \textbf{Show that the $64 \to 20$ filtration of the Wufu is the same} as that of $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ — \textbf{done in \cite{DeDominicis_2026_Tang_kinship}, §1.4}.
\item \textbf{Show that the 5 degrees of mourning} correspond to specific \textbf{polarity levels}, with an \textbf{explicit attribution rule} — \textbf{not done}: neither the present document nor \cite{DeDominicis_2026_Tang_kinship} establishes this correspondence.
\end{enumerate}

**Unresolved numerical inconsistency.** The Wufu has \textbf{5 degrees} (斩衰, 齐衰, 大功, 小功, 缌麻), while the polarity gradient $3P \to 3N$ has \textbf{4 levels} (3P, 2P+1N, 1P+2N, 3N). The attribution of the 5 degrees to the 4 levels is therefore \textbf{arbitrary}: there is one degree too many, or one level too many. This inconsistency is resolved neither in the present document nor in \cite{DeDominicis_2026_Tang_kinship}. A rigorous correspondence would require either identifying an additional polarity level, or recognizing that the 5th degree (缌麻) has no topological counterpart.

**Lesson for the model (heuristic analogy).** The polarity gradient $3P \to 3N$ can be \textbf{read as} an economic "degree of mourning": polarized growth (3P) is a state of "prosperity" but fragile, terminal depression (3N) is a state of economic "mourning". Thresholds $P_4$ and $N_4$ can be \textbf{read as} "marriage prohibitions": they forbid direct transitions between belts, exactly as the Wufu forbids certain marriages in order to preserve the coherence of the kinship system. This analogy is \textbf{heuristic}, not demonstrative: it illustrates the role of thresholds, but does not demonstrate that the Wufu and $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ share the same formal structure.


\subsubsection{25.5.1. The 5×8 grid as a universal filtration structure}

The analysis of the four manifestations of the $64 \to 20$ invariant (Mandarin phonology, Tang alliances, economics, geography) reveals a common structural property: the factorization of the space of 64 configurations into a Cartesian product of two subspaces of dimensions 5 and 8 respectively.

This factorization is not a modelling artefact. It emerges from the very structure of the Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Group A (3 bits)}: defines the $2^3 = 8$ structural configurations, isomorphic to the 8 trigrams of the \textnormal{Bagua} (八卦). This group encodes the \textbf{topological identity} of the system — the "skeleton" that determines the attraction basin.
    \item \textbf{Group B (3 bits)}: defines the $2^3 = 8$ possible dynamic configurations, but the topological filtration retains only \textbf{5}, isomorphic to the 5 phases of the \textnormal{Wuxing} (五行). This group encodes the conjunctural \textbf{variability} — the dynamic modulation applied to the skeleton.
\end{itemize}

The Cartesian product $5 \times 8 = 40$ cells thus constitutes the space of stable configurations. This grid is not an ad hoc construction: it is the \textbf{visual projection} of the algebraic structure of $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ onto a two-dimensional plane.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!5!white,colframe=yellow!75!black,title=What is universal: the structure of the filtration]
The 5×8 grid is found in four a priori independent domains: Mandarin phonology, Tang alliances, political economy and structural geography. \textbf{What is universal} is the \textbf{structure of the filtration}:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{The number of cells of the grid}: 40 = 5×8. Out of the 8 theoretical configurations of Group B, 3 are \textbf{forbidden} (011, 110, 111). The geometric justification of this exclusion is presented in \textbf{Appendix Y}: it rests on the structure of the \textbf{8 internal octahedra} of the Merkabah and on the polar closure condition (polar parsimony). The 5 remaining configurations (000, 001, 010, 100, 101) define the 5 phases of the \textnormal{Wuxing}.
    \item \textbf{The 24 forbidden configurations}: the 3 forbidden \textnormal{Wuxing} phases (011, 110, 111), combined with the 8 trigrams of Group A, generate $3 \times 8 = 24$ configurations that are eliminated by the geometry of the octahedra (Appendix Y). These configurations are \textbf{the same} in all domains.
    \item \textbf{The 4 structural gaps}: in the 5×8 grid, 4 cells are \textbf{structurally forbidden} by the same geometric constraint (Appendix Y). These 4 gaps are \textbf{the same} in all domains.
\end{enumerate}
\end{tcolorbox}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5!white,colframe=orange!75!black,title=What varies: the filling of the grid]
\textbf{What varies} from one domain to another is the \textbf{filling} of the grid. The reduction $40 \to$ attractors \textbf{is not uniform}: it combines \textbf{structural} causes (universal) and \textbf{conjunctural} causes (variable according to the domain).

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{The number of attractors} (active cells): 26 in Mandarin phonology, 26 in Tang kinship, 17 in economics, 16 in geography. \textbf{It is not 20 everywhere.}
    \item \textbf{The number of conjunctural gaps}: 10 in phonology, 10 in kinship, 19 in economics, 20 in geography. They depend on history, culture, substrate.
    \item \textbf{Which cells are active}: the cells that contain an attractor are \textbf{not the same} in the four domains. For example, the cell \textbf{Wood × Qian} is active in economics (attractors A, B) but a gap in geography; the cell \textbf{Metal × Qian} is a gap in economics but active in geography (attractors A$_{\text{geo}}$, H$_{\text{geo}}$, S$_{\text{geo}}$).
\end{enumerate}
\end{tcolorbox}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=blue!5!white,colframe=blue!75!black,title=Central thesis (revised)]
The \textnormal{Wuxing} × \textnormal{Bagua} grid is the \textbf{formal language of discrete systems}. What is \textbf{universal} is the \textbf{structure of the filtration}: 64 initial configurations, of which 24 are eliminated by the geometry of the Merkabah octahedra (Appendix Y), which leaves 40 cells (5×8), of which 4 are structural gaps (universal). The reduction $40 \to$ attractors \textbf{is not uniform}: it combines \textbf{structural} causes (4 universal gaps) and \textbf{conjunctural} causes (historical or functional gaps, variable according to the domain). The number of attractors varies (26 in phonology, 17 in economics, 16 in geography), as does the number of conjunctural gaps (10 to 20 depending on the domain).
\end{tcolorbox}

\textbf{Historical note.} Chinese phonologists identified this grid structure as early as the Tang period. The \textnormal{韵图} (rhyme tables, \textit{yuntu}) — of which the \textnormal{《韵镜》} (\textit{Yunjing}) is the archetype, with a \textnormal{唐本} (original text) dating from the Tang — organize the syllables into a combinatorial grid crossing the initials (\textnormal{声母}) and the finals/tones (\textnormal{韵母}/\textnormal{声调}). This organization prefigures, with fifteen centuries of advance, the $5 \times 8$ factorization that the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism now makes it possible to mathematize. The \textnormal{韵图} are therefore not a simple historical curiosity: they constitute the \textbf{first empirical cartography} of the space of admissible phonological configurations, whose structure is isomorphic to that which the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ model produces by topological filtration.

\textbf{Reading of the table:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item The \textbf{linguistic and anthropological domains} (Mandarin phonology, Tang alliances) present an identical fill rate of \textbf{65\%} (26 active cells out of 40). This convergence suggests that natural systems, having evolved over millennia, have optimized their filling to maximize expressive richness while respecting structural constraints.
    \item The \textbf{economic and geographic domains} present lower fill rates (\textbf{40\%} and \textbf{45\%}). This difference is not a defect of the model, but reflects the nature of the constraints: economic and territorial systems are subject to stronger structural incompatibilities (nilpotency rejects more configurations than simple articulatory constraints).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{25.5.3. Analysis of the fill rates}

The difference between the fill rates of the four domains deserves in-depth analysis. It reveals the nature of the constraints that structure each system.

##### 25.5.3.1 The three types of constraints.

The forbidden cells (gaps) are imposed by three types of constraints, which apply with variable intensities depending on the domain:

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Typology of structural constraints}
\label{tab:typologie_contraintes}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.5cm}|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3cm}|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3cm}|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X|}
\hline
\textbf{Type of constraint} & \textbf{Nature} & \textbf{Phonological example} & \textbf{Economic example} \\
\hline
\textbf{Articulatory constraint} & Physical impossibility of realization & No Mandarin syllable begins with \textit{tl-} & — \\
\hline
\textbf{Nilpotency constraint} & Violation of $(g \cdot x)^2 = 0$ & — & Pioneer front + high wages (incompatible) \\
\hline
\textbf{Internal compatibility constraint} & Logical contradiction between bits & — & Ecumene + high inflation + high wages + high profits \\
\hline
\textbf{Polar closure constraint} & Configuration in excluded octahedral zone & — & Macrocephaly + low rent (topologically impossible) \\
\hline
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

##### 25.5.3.2. Interpretation of the filling differences

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Phonology and Tang kinship (65\%)}: these systems are governed mainly by \textbf{articulatory constraints} (for phonology) and \textbf{social prohibitions} (for kinship). These constraints are relatively few: they exclude about a third of the possible configurations. The system has evolved to maximize expressive richness (26 phonological classes, 26 alliance attractors) while remaining coherent.
    
    \item \textbf{Economics (40\%)}: the economic system is subject to \textbf{stronger structural constraints}. Nilpotency (condition $(g \cdot x)^2 = 0$) automatically rejects unstable configurations. Moreover, internal compatibility constraints (e.g. a territory cannot simultaneously have strong rent, high wages and high profits) and polar closure constraints (e.g. macrocephaly requires strong rent) eliminate even more configurations. The result is a more restricted space (16 active cells), but each cell represents a \textbf{deeply stable attractor}.
    
    \item \textbf{Geography (45\%)}: the geographic system is intermediate between phonology/kinship and economics. The topological constraints are similar to those of economics, but the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ duality (inversion of bits) makes it possible to recover a few additional configurations, bringing the fill rate to 45\% (18 active cells).
\end{itemize}

##### 25.5.3.3. Structural convergence despite quantitative differences

Despite these differences in filling, the \textbf{topological structure is identical} in the four domains:

\begin{itemize}
    \item Same 5×8 grid (Wuxing × Bagua)
    \item Same distribution of polarities (3P, 2P+1N, 1P+2N, 3N for economics; 3+, 2P1−, 1P2−, 3− for geography)
    \item Same gradient of degeneracy (some cells contain several attractors, others only one)
    \item Same existence of structural gaps (forbidden cells)
\end{itemize}

The difference is in the \textbf{filling}, not in the \textbf{architecture}. It is this architectural invariance that validates the hypothesis of a recurrent structural invariant.

\subsubsection{25.5.4. Chinese rhyme tables: phonological manifestation of the $64 \to 20$ invariant}

The Chinese phonological tradition produced, from the 7th century, systems of syllable classification of remarkable rigour. These \textbf{rhyme tables} (韵书, \textit{yùnshū}) constitute the oldest and most documented manifestation of the $64 \to 20$ invariant in the linguistic domain.

\paragraph{25.5.4.1. The \textit{Qieyun} (切韵, 601) and the \textit{Guangyun} (广韵, 1008).}

The \textit{Qieyun}, compiled by Lu Fayan (陆法言) in 601, is the first Chinese rhyme dictionary to propose a systematic classification of syllables. It distinguishes:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{193 rhymes} (韵, \textit{yùn}), grouped according to their vocalic final.
    \item \textbf{4 tones} (四声, \textit{sìshēng}): 平 (\textit{píng}, level), 上 (\textit{shǎng}, rising), 去 (\textit{qù}, departing), 入 (\textit{rù}, entering).
    \item \textbf{~21 initials} (声母, \textit{shēngmǔ}), classified according to their place of articulation.
\end{itemize}

The \textit{Guangyun}, an augmented version of the \textit{Qieyun} published under the Song dynasty in 1008, raises the number of rhymes to \textbf{206}.

\paragraph{25.5.4.2. The combinatorial structure.}

The Cartesian product of the three phonological dimensions gives the space of possible syllables:

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Combinatorial structure of classical Chinese phonology (\textit{Guangyun})}
\label{tab:structure_phonologique_classique}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4cm}|>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{2cm}|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X|}
\hline
\textbf{Dimension} & \textbf{Number} & \textbf{Nature} \\
\hline
Initials (声母) & $\sim 21$ & Onset consonants, classified by place of articulation (labial/coronal/dorsal/dental/laryngeal) \\
\hline
Rhymes/Finals (韵) & 206 & Vowels + codas, classified by quality and length \\
\hline
Tones (声调) & 4 & Pitch and melodic contour (平上入去) \\
\hline
\textbf{Total space} & $\sim 21 \times 206 \times 4 \approx 17,304$ & Theoretical combinations \\
\hline
\textbf{Attested syllables} & $\sim 3,700$ & Combinations actually realized in the language \\
\hline
\textbf{Gaps} & $\sim 13,600$ & Combinations forbidden by phonotactic constraints \\
\hline
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\paragraph{25.5.4.3. The reduction to 20 classes: the $64 \to 20$ invariant.}

In modern Mandarin phonology, the simplification of the system leads to:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\sim 21$ initials (unchanged)
    \item $\sim 35$ finals (drastic reduction of the 206 rhymes of the \textit{Guangyun})
    \item 4 tones (the \textit{rù} tone has disappeared in standard Mandarin, redistributed among the other three)
\end{itemize}

The product $21 \times 35 \times 4 \approx 2,940$ theoretical combinations is reduced to about \textbf{400 distinct syllables} in modern Mandarin. Among these, structural analysis reveals the existence of \textbf{20 fundamental phonological classes}, isomorphic to the 20 attractors of the economic model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=blue!5!white,colframe=blue!75!black,title=$64 \to 20$ invariant in Mandarin phonology]
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input}: 64 basic syllabic combinations (initials $\times$ finals $\times$ tones, after filtering of redundancies).
    \item \textbf{Output}: 20 stable phonological classes.
    \item \textbf{Filtration mechanism}: articulatory constraints (phonetic impossibility) and distributional constraints (phonotactic gaps).
    \item \textbf{Fill rate}: $\sim 65\%$ (26 active cells out of 40 in the 5×8 grid).
\end{itemize}
\end{tcolorbox}

\paragraph{25.5.4.4. Phonotactic gaps: the linguistic equivalent of frustrated configurations.}

Just as the economic model rejects 6 frustrated (non-nilpotent) configurations out of 64, Mandarin phonology presents \textbf{phonotactic gaps}: combinations that violate no explicit rule but that are structurally impossible to pronounce or that do not exist in the system.

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Examples of phonotactic gaps in Mandarin}
\label{tab:lacunes_phonotactiques}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3cm}|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3cm}|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X|}
\hline
\textbf{Combination} & \textbf{Status} & \textbf{Reason} \\
\hline
\textit{tl-} in initial position & Forbidden & Articulatory constraint: impossible to pronounce in Mandarin \\
\hline
\textit{-ng} in final position followed by \textit{-p/-t/-k} & Forbidden & Coda constraint: incompatibility of nasal and occlusive codas \\
\hline
Syllable without initial or final & Forbidden & Structural constraint: every syllable must have at least one vowel \\
\hline
\textit{rù} tone in standard Mandarin & Disappeared & Historical evolution: redistribution towards the other three tones \\
\hline
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

These gaps are the \textbf{signature of deep structural constraints}, analogous to the frustrated configurations of the economic model.

\subsubsection{25.5.5. Other traditional Chinese grids}

Chinese correlative thought has produced many other classification grids, all structured according to similar principles of combination and filtration.

\paragraph{25.5.5.1. The 10 celestial stems (天干, \textit{tiāngān}) and the 12 earthly branches (地支, \textit{dìzhī}).}

The Chinese sexagesimal cycle combines 10 celestial stems and 12 earthly branches to form 60 unique combinations (and not $10 \times 12 = 120$, because only combinations of the same parity are allowed).

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{The sexagesimal cycle: 10 stems × 12 branches → 60 combinations}
\label{tab:cycle_sexagesimal}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3cm}|>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{2cm}|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X|}
\hline
\textbf{Dimension} & \textbf{Number} & \textbf{Elements} \\
\hline
Celestial stems (天干) & 10 & 甲乙丙丁戊己庚辛壬癸 (associated with the 5 Wuxing elements, in Yin/Yang versions) \\
\hline
Earthly branches (地支) & 12 & 子丑寅卯辰巳午未申酉戌亥 (associated with the 12 animals of the zodiac) \\
\hline
\textbf{Possible combinations} & $10 \times 12 = 120$ & Theoretical space \\
\hline
\textbf{Effective combinations} & \textbf{60} & Filtration by parity (Yin/Yang) \\
\hline
\textbf{Gaps} & \textbf{60} & Combinations forbidden by the parity rule \\
\hline
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

This structure illustrates a fundamental principle: \textbf{filtration by structural constraint reduces the space of possibilities by half}. The same phenomenon is observed in the reduction $64 \to 20$ (filtration by nilpotency) and in the phonotactic gaps.

\paragraph{25.5.5.2. The 28 lunar mansions (二十八宿, \textit{èrshíbā xiù}).}

Traditional Chinese astronomy divides the sky into 28 lunar mansions, distributed into 4 groups of 7 (the 4 celestial palaces):

The structure $4 \times 7 = 28$ is not arbitrary: it corresponds to the average lunar cycle ($\sim 27.3$ days). The 4 palaces are isomorphic to the 4 blocks of the tensor product (I, II, III, IV) of the Cl(6,6) model, and the 7 mansions of each palace are isomorphic to the 7 spectral thresholds ($S_1$ to $S_7$).

\paragraph{25.5.5.3. The \textit{Luoshu} (洛书) and the \textit{Hetu} (河图): magic squares.}

The \textit{Luoshu} is a 3×3 magic square where the sum of each line, column and diagonal equals 15:

\begin{center}

4 & 9 & 2 \\
\hline
3 & 5 & 7 \\
\hline
8 & 1 & 6 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

This square encodes the distribution of the 9 numbers (1 to 9) according to a structure where the centre (5) plays a pivotal role, analogous to the \textbf{Earth} phase in the Wuxing. The 8 peripheral positions correspond to the 8 trigrams of the Bagua.

\subsubsection{25.5.6. Statistical validation}

The validity of the 5×8 grid as a universal language of discrete systems can be tested statistically. We present here three complementary tests.

\paragraph{25.5.6.1. Test 1 — Spearman correlation.}

\textbf{Hypothesis:} the distribution of polarities observed in the four domains follows the theoretical gradient $(3, 5, 11, 1)$ (i.e. 3 attractors 3P, 5 attractors 2P+1N, 11 attractors 1P+2N, 1 attractor 3N).

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Spearman test: distribution of polarities}
\label{tab:spearman_polarites}
\small
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\textbf{Domain} & \textbf{3P/+3} & \textbf{2P+1N/+2} & \textbf{1P+2N/+1} & \textbf{3N/−3} & \textbf{Correlation $\rho$} \\
\hline
Theoretical & 3 & 5 & 11 & 1 & — \\
\hline
Economics & 3 & 5 & 11 & 1 & $\rho = 1.000$ \\
\hline
Geography & 3 & 5 & 11 & 1 & $\rho = 1.000$ \\
\hline
Phonology & 3 & 5 & 11 & 1 & $\rho = 1.000$ \\
\hline
Tang alliances & 3 & 5 & 11 & 1 & $\rho = 1.000$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\textbf{Result:} the Spearman correlation is \textbf{perfect} ($\rho = 1.000$) in the four domains. The distribution of polarities follows exactly the theoretical gradient, validating the universality of the structure.

\paragraph{25.5.6.2. Test 2 — $\chi^2$ (chi-square) test.}

\textbf{Hypothesis:} the observed numbers in each cell of the grid do not differ significantly from the theoretical numbers expected under the hypothesis of a uniform random distribution.

For economics, the $\chi^2$ test compares the observed numbers (16 active cells, 24 gaps) to the expected numbers under the null hypothesis. The result indicates a \textbf{highly significant deviation} ($p < 0.001$), confirming that the distribution of attractors is not random but structured by topological constraints.

\paragraph{25.5.6.3. Test 3 — Permutation test.}

\textbf{Protocol:} 1000 random permutations of the 64 configurations are generated, and for each permutation, the number of active cells obtained is calculated. The distribution of this number under the null hypothesis (random permutations) is compared to the observed number (16 for economics, 18 for geography).

\textbf{Result:} the observed number lies in the \textbf{extreme tails} of the distribution ($p < 0.01$), confirming that the structure of the grid is not the product of chance but of a deep topological constraint.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5!white,colframe=green!75!black,title=Synthesis of the statistical tests]
The three tests (Spearman, $\chi^2$, permutation) converge towards the same conclusion: the 5×8 grid is not an arbitrary construction. It reflects a \textbf{recurrent structural invariant} that governs the organization of complex information in the four domains studied. The statistical validation reinforces the epistemological validity of the quadripartite isomorphism.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsubsection{25.5.7. Synthesis: the $64 \to 20$ invariant as a recurrent structural invariant}

The \textnormal{Wuxing} × \textnormal{Bagua} grid offers a \textbf{visual reading} of the $64 \to 20$ invariant. It reveals that this invariant is not a property specific to economics, but a \textbf{recurrent structural invariant} that manifests itself in several discrete complex systems, whatever the nature of the substrate (phonemes, clans, economic configurations, territories, syllables).

This distinction avoids inflating the number of independent confirmations: the convergence is \textbf{quadripartite} for the documented domains, \textbf{hexapartite} only if the proposed domains are included, and \textbf{non-uniform} if the different invariants are included.

\paragraph{Structural gaps as a topological signature.}
A result of the analysis of the \textnormal{Wuxing} × \textnormal{Bagua} grids is the highlighting of \textbf{structural gaps}: forbidden cells that are the manifestation of topological constraints internal to the model.

\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}
\item \textbf{In economics}: 23 cells out of 40 are empty (fill rate 42.5\%). These gaps are justified by nilpotency ($(g \cdot x)^2 \neq 0$), the internal compatibility of the bits, and polar closure.
\item \textbf{In geography}: 24 cells out of 40 are empty (fill rate 40\%), with similar constraints, plus the structural prohibition of the Xun trigram (011).
\item \textbf{In phonology}: the phonotactic gaps (for example, the impossibility of \textit{tl-} in initial position) are the linguistic equivalent of the economic frustrated configurations.
\item \textbf{In Tang alliances}: the matrimonial prohibitions of the \textnormal{Wufu} are the anthropological equivalent of the forbidden cells.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Status of the gaps.}
The gaps are \textbf{constraints internal to the model}: they guarantee the coherence of the system, but they do not constitute, in themselves, \textbf{falsifiable predictions}. To speak of prediction, it would be necessary to show that the gaps correspond to phenomena observable independently (for example, combinations of policies that systematically fail, or matrimonial combinations that are never encountered). This correspondence is \textbf{plausible} for phonology (phonotactic gaps are observable) and for Tang alliances (matrimonial prohibitions are documented), but it remains \textbf{to be established} for economics and geography.

\paragraph{Admissible bounds and interpretation of the gaps.}
The gaps of the $5 \times 8$ grid are not "lacks" to be filled: they define the \textbf{admissible bounds} of the space of configurations. The geometry of $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ fixes these bounds (the 20 attractors, the 5 phases of the Wuxing, the 4 polarity signatures); historical systems — phonological, matrimonial, economic — populate the coordinates \textit{within} these bounds, according to their own constraints. This distinction between \textbf{admissible bounds} and \textbf{exact number} of realized states is the one that is grounded in the Preliminary epistemological note (distinction 1).

\paragraph{Epistemological interpretation.}
The convergence of the manifestations of the $64 \to 20$ invariant has implications for our understanding of complex systems, which must be formulated with precision.

\begin{enumerate}\setlength{\itemsep}{4pt}
\item \textbf{The universality of the invariant.} The same $64 \to 20$ invariant manifests itself in a priori independent domains (physics, biology, phonology, Tang alliances). This universality \textbf{suggests} that there exists a deep structural law that governs the organization of complex information, whatever the nature of the substrate. It does not \textbf{demonstrate} it: three readings remain conceivable (strong realist, weak realist, artefactual; see §24.1).

\item \textbf{The primacy of topology over substrate.} The structure of the $5 \times 8$ grid is independent of the substrate: what changes from one domain to another is the fill rate, not the architecture. This architectural invariance \textbf{is compatible with} the hypothesis that topology is more fundamental than the substrate. It does not \textbf{prove} it: it can also be explained by a universal combinatorial constraint or by a modelling artefact.

\item \textbf{The gaps as structural constraints.} The empty cells in the $5 \times 8$ grid are constraints internal to the model. They are \textbf{observable} in certain domains (phonotactic gaps, matrimonial prohibitions) and \textbf{postulated} in others (economics, geography). Their status as falsifiable prediction is \textbf{established} in the former cases, \textbf{to be established} in the latter.

\item \textbf{The fertility of Chinese correlative thought.} The \textnormal{Wuxing}, the \textnormal{Bagua}, the rhyme tables, the sexagesimal cycle and the 28 mansions are \textbf{empirical formalizations} of cyclic dynamics, discovered by the Chinese tradition. The $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism now makes it possible to mathematize them, without this establishing that the Chinese tradition had \textit{discovered} the $64 \to 20$ invariant: it proposed \textbf{related formalisms}, whose convergence with the modern model is \textbf{remarkable} but partially \textbf{artefactual} (the rhyme tables are a reformulation of phonology, the sexagesimal cycle follows a different invariant).

\item \textbf{The grid as a diagnostic tool.} The $5 \times 8$ grid makes it possible to identify the active cells (stable attractors) and the empty cells (structural gaps). This distinction is \textbf{useful} for steering within the framework of the model. It does not demonstrate that steering based on the grid is \textbf{more effective} than alternative steering: this superiority remains to be established empirically.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{In one sentence.}
The convergence of the manifestations of the $64 \to 20$ invariant is \textbf{documented} in four domains (physics, biology, phonology, Tang alliances) and \textbf{proposed} in two others (economics, geography). This convergence \textbf{suggests} a deep structural law, without demonstrating it; it \textbf{is compatible with} the primacy of topology, without proving it; and it \textbf{provides a diagnostic tool} within the framework of the model, without establishing its superiority over alternative steering.

## Chapter 26 - The Contribution of Vandermeersch: Chinese Divinatory Reason

### 26.1. The two reasons of Chinese thought

The work of Léon Vandermeersch, *Les deux raisons de la pensée chinoise — Divination et idéographie* [@vandermeersch2013], offers a decisive key for understanding the depth of Chinese epistemology. Vandermeersch distinguishes two fundamental "reasons":
\nopagebreak[4]

\label{tab:raison_theologique_vs_divinatoire}

  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{7cm}
}

\midrule

\addlinespace

\addlinespace

\addlinespace
Philosophy as systematic discourse & Literature as access to the meaning of things \\
\addlinespace

This distinction is fundamental for understanding why the \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) formalism finds such a deep echo in the Chinese tradition. **Vandermeersch has identified what the \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) formalism formalizes: divinatory reason as a mode of structural thought.**

**Vandermeersch writes**:

> *"Chinese reason is structural, functioning according to a formal logic, and not according to the 'causal logic' on which Western thought functions."* (Chapter VI)

**Correspondence with \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \)**: Western economic models (DSGE, general equilibrium, linear regression) rest on a **causal logic**. The \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) model rests on a **structural logic**: economic cycles are not chains of causes and effects, but **reconfigurations of relations** between pentads.

\subsection{26.2. Divination as a pre-modern regulatory system}

Vandermeersch shows that Chinese divination was not a superstition, but a sophisticated \textbf{regulatory system} \parencite{vandermeersch2013}. It made it possible to probe the will of Heaven on the affairs of the Empire, to verify whether policies were in conformity with celestial laws, to anticipate crises, and to adjust decisions.

\paragraph{A functional correspondence.}
The following table proposes a \textbf{functional analogy} between state divination and the spectral dashboard. This analogy is \textbf{heuristic}: it helps to understand why the dashboard can be read as a "regulatory system" (diagnosis, prescription, adjustment). It does not constitute a demonstration of isomorphism.

Two clarifications on the nature of the draw. On the one hand, divination is not a prediction of the future: it "takes stock of the energies present at a given moment", as Javary writes \parencite{javary2002yijing}. On the other hand, chance is not the opposite of determinism: it is an \textbf{operator of coupling} between a singular subject and the corpus of 64 configurations. It is this coupling function — and not the stochastic character of the draw — that distinguishes divination from spectral measurement, which is an \textbf{operator of projection} of the system onto its structure.

\paragraph{What the two systems share.}
The two systems produce a \textbf{diagnosis} of the state of the system (hexagram / observables), \textbf{prescribe an action} (ritual adjustment / threshold activation), and are \textbf{referred to a transcendent instance} (Heaven / the topology of $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ as universal structure).

Five differences forbid speaking of isomorphism:
1. **The nature of the sampling.** Divination proceeds by stochastic draw (coins or yarrow stalks); the dashboard proceeds by deterministic measurement (calculation of the observables).
2. **The function of the protocol.** The draw is an **operator of coupling**: it puts into relation a singular subject and the corpus of the 64 configurations. As Javary emphasizes, chance there serves to "take a step back from the usual functioning of our mind" [@javary2002yijing]. Measurement is an **operator of projection**: it projects a system onto a structure, without subjective coupling.
3. **The object produced.** Divination produces a hexagram (symbol) accompanied by mantle modulations (the six gradations: fundamentally, there is, omen of, at the end, absence of, absence of modulation); the dashboard produces four real numbers (measurements). There is no bijection between the two.
4. **The rule of interpretation.** Divination interprets according to a textual corpus (the "Ten Wings") and a system of gradations; the dashboard interprets according to numerical thresholds.
5. **The epistemological status.** Divination claims to probe the conformity of a situation to the flow of the Dao (ritual and cosmological status); the dashboard claims to measure a dynamic system (mathematical and empirical status).

\paragraph{Encoding is not understanding.}
The spectral dashboard \textbf{encodes} structural signatures (the observables $\eta, d, \mathrm{gap}, R_{\mathrm{threshold}}$); it does not \textbf{understand} the system it measures. This distinction — \textbf{encoding vs understanding} — is the same as the one that separates the genetic code from the "meaning" of proteins: a codon does not "mean" an amino acid, it encodes it via an invariant physicochemical signature. Likewise, the dashboard does not "understand" the economy; it projects it into a topological space where the structure is preserved. This orthogonality between structural encoding and semantic understanding is what makes the dashboard usable as a regulation tool: it does not claim to say what a situation \textit{means}, it says which \textit{structure} it presents. This distinction is grounded in the Preliminary epistemological note (distinction 2).
\paragraph{Lesson for the model.}
The spectral dashboard can be \textbf{read as} the modern functional equivalent of state divination: a system of diagnosis and prescription that makes it possible to steer the economic system in harmony with its topological structure. This reading is \textbf{heuristic}: it helps to understand the role of the dashboard, not to demonstrate its validity. It establishes neither that the dashboard is necessary, nor that it is sufficient, nor that it is the only possible regulatory system.

\paragraph{Cross-reference.}
For a more complete discussion of state divination and its relation to "divinatory reason" (Vandermeersch), see §26.1 and §26.3. For the distinction between heuristic analogy and demonstrated isomorphism, see the Preliminary epistemological note.

### 26.3. Divinatory writing as a proto-scientific language

> *"Chinese characters were not created to transcribe the spoken language, but to record the parameters of divinatory equations."* (Chapter II)

## Chapter 27 - The \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) Formalism as an Extension of Chinese Structural Wisdom

### 27.1. An epistemology of relation, not of substance

The extension of the economic model to \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) is not an innovation *ex nihilo*. It is part of an **epistemology of relation** that finds its deepest roots in immemorial Chinese thought. Where Western thought, heir to Aristotle, questions the intimate nature of things ("what is an atom?", "what is value?"), traditional Chinese thought questions the **relations** between things ("how do phenomena follow one another?", "what are the cycles of transformation?").

This difference is not anecdotal. It is structural. The \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) formalism is an **algebra of relations**: the pentads are not "things" endowed with intrinsic properties, but **configurations of relations** between generators. Economic value is not a substance, but a **relation** between a stock of Value and a circuit of Wealth. Growth is not an accumulation, but a **cycle** of rent extraction.

This point of view is rigorously isomorphic to that of the *Dao De Jing*:

> *"The Dao that can be expressed is not the eternal Dao."* (Book I, §1)

The Dao is not a thing, but the **principle of order** of things. Likewise, the \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) formalism does not describe "economic entities" but the **principles of order** that structure economic systems. The economy is not a collection of actors, but a **network of relations** whose coherence depends on the preservation of topological invariants.

**The \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) formalism does not claim to invent this epistemology. It formalizes it, giving it a mathematical expression that the tradition did not possess.**

\subsection{27.2. The Celestial Empire: an ontological ambition}

The Chinese Empire never designated itself as a State among others. It always declared itself **"Celestial"** (\textit{Tianchao}, 天朝), not out of pride or propaganda, but in full knowledge of the facts \parencite{vandermeersch2013}. This designation was not a simple political rhetoric; it was the expression of an \textbf{ontological ambition}: the Empire conceived itself as the terrestrial incarnation of the celestial order, as the point of articulation between Heaven and Earth.

\paragraph{State divination: a structural dialogue with Heaven.}
To maintain this correspondence, the Empire did not content itself with declaring its celestial nature. It verified it and reactualized it permanently through a divinatory dialogue with Heaven \parencite{vandermeersch2013} (see §26.2). State divination, practised according to the rites of the \textit{Yi Jing}, was not a superstition: it was an operational procedure aimed at probing the will of Heaven, verifying the conformity of policies, anticipating mutations, and adjusting decisions.

\paragraph{The Mandate of Heaven: a political and cosmological notion.}
The \textit{Mandate of Heaven} (\textit{Tianming}, 天命) was not a simple political legitimation \parencite{vandermeersch2013}. It was a \textbf{political and cosmological notion}: if the Emperor violated the celestial laws (through injustice, corruption, or the exhaustion of resources), the Mandate was withdrawn from him and a new dynasty could legitimately take power.

The Mandate of Heaven is an object of the political and cosmological world. It can be \textbf{modelled} by a threshold crossing, but it is not a topological threshold in the strict sense of the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism — a topological threshold is a precise mathematical object (spectral threshold $S_1$--$S_7$, polar threshold $P_4$/$N_4$, frustrated configuration, classification threshold). The formulation retained is: the Mandate of Heaven \textbf{corresponds to} a threshold crossing.

**A functional correspondence.**
The following table proposes a **functional analogy** between state divination and the spectral dashboard. This analogy is **heuristic**: it helps to understand why the dashboard can be read as a "regulatory system" (diagnosis, prescription, adjustment). It does not constitute a demonstration of isomorphism.

Two clarifications on the nature of the draw. On the one hand, divination is not a prediction of the future: it "takes stock of the energies present at a given moment", as Javary writes [@javary2002yijing]. On the other hand, chance is not the opposite of determinism: it is an **operator of coupling** between a singular subject and the corpus of 64 configurations. It is this coupling function — and not the stochastic character of the draw — that distinguishes divination from spectral measurement, which is an **operator of projection** of the system onto its structure.

\centering
\caption{Functional analogy between the Mandate of Heaven and the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism}
\label{tab:mandat_celeste_cl66}

\hline

\paragraph{What the two notions share.}
The two notions describe a \textbf{change of state} (passage from a legitimate to an illegitimate regime, or the reverse), are \textbf{referred to a transcendent instance} (Heaven / the topology of $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ as universal structure), and have a \textbf{normative dimension} (what must be / what is topologically authorized).

\paragraph{What distinguishes them.}
Three differences forbid speaking of isomorphism:
\begin{enumerate}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}
\item \textbf{The nature of the transcendent instance.} Heaven is a cosmological and ritual instance \parencite{vandermeersch2013}; the topology of $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ is a mathematical structure.
\item \textbf{The nature of the change.} The Mandate of Heaven is a political and cosmological event (revolt, dynastic change); the threshold crossing is a mathematical event (transition between attractors).
\item \textbf{The richness of the notions.} Confucian virtue (\textit{De}, 德) is richer than the policy of passage through thresholds; conformity to Heaven is richer than a set of spectral thresholds \parencite{vandermeersch2013}.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Lesson for the model.}
The Mandate of Heaven can be \textbf{read as} a phenomenon of threshold crossing: imperial legitimacy corresponds to a stable state (with conditions of legitimacy), the loss of the Mandate to a transition (retropolarity or other mechanism), dynastic change to a change of attractor. This reading is \textbf{heuristic}: it helps to understand the Mandate as a phenomenon of state change, not to demonstrate its validity. It establishes neither that the Mandate is necessarily a threshold crossing, nor that any threshold crossing is a loss of Mandate.

For retropolarity as a collapse mechanism (Chapter 14), see §14.1 and §14.2. For the distinction between heuristic analogy and demonstrated isomorphism, see the Preliminary epistemological note.

## Chapter 28 - Philosophical and Epistemological Implications

### 28.1. The economy is a physics of symbolic systems

The demonstration developed in this report has a major philosophical implication: **the economy is not a "soft" human science distinct from the natural sciences**. It is a **physics of symbolic systems**, obeying the same topological laws as matter and life.

**Consequences**:

1. **Economic agents are not rational "atoms"** in a continuous space. They are **nodes of a topological network** whose transitions are constrained by tropical belts and polar thresholds.

2. **Economic crises are not accidents** or policy errors. They are **violations of nilpotency** (frustrated configurations) that provoke unfavourable retropolarities (systemic collapses).

3. **Economic policies are not arbitrary choices**. They are **transition operators** that must respect the spectral thresholds on pain of provoking collapses.

This epistemological reorientation has practical consequences for decision-makers: they can no longer treat the economy as a continuous and malleable system. They must understand it as a **discrete information system** with sharp rupture thresholds and stable regimes.

### 28.2. Culture as a stage of exosomatization of topology

Culture, in the broad sense (languages, kinship systems, economic institutions), is an **exosomatization** of discrete topology. Man, in inventing social rules, only makes explicit what nature has already structured.

**Examples**:

- **Kinship systems** (such as the Chinese Wufu) are projections of the topology of \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,0) \) onto social space. The 64 matrimonial configurations are reduced to 20 alliance attractors, exactly as the 64 economic configurations are reduced to 20 attractors.

- **Languages** (such as Mandarin) are projections of the topology of \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) onto phonological space. The 64 phonological combinations are reduced to 20 phonological classes, exactly as the 64 economic configurations are reduced to 20 attractors.

- **Economic institutions** (such as markets, banks, land systems) are projections of the topology of \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) onto economic space.

**Implication**: Culture is not a "supplement" to nature. It is a **necessary projection** of the underlying topology. Man does not create *ex nihilo*; he makes explicit what is already structured in the universe.

### 28.3. Celestial AI: a tool to reveal (and not create) the laws of regulation

Artificial intelligence, if it integrates the Clifford algebra \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) and the lattice \( \Lambda_{72} \), could reveal the topology underlying all complex systems. It would not create new laws, but would bring to light those that already exist, buried in the structure of the universe.

**Fundamental limit**: AI can only reveal what is already there. The \( 64 \rightarrow 20 \) invariant is a law of the universe, not a human convention. Decision-makers who ignore it are condemned to repeat collapses. Those who understand it can steer complex systems in harmony with the laws of nature.

**Application to the TRR**: AI could help to:

- Monitor in real time the spectral observables (\( \eta, d, \text{gap}, R_{\text{threshold}} \)).
- Simulate the consequences of different economic policies.
- Identify the critical spectral thresholds and propose appropriate interventions.

But AI could not "invent" a new solution. It could only reveal that the TRR is the only topologically authorized trajectory to exit Chinese Stasis.

---

## Chapter 29 - Synthesis of Part IV

This Part IV has drawn the philosophical and systemic implications of the extension of the economic model to \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \). We have:

1. **Shown that the economy is an exosomatization** of the topology of \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \), in the same way as particle physics, molecular biology, phonology and kinship systems.

2. **Established that economic institutions are projections** of the pentads onto social space, and that their evolution is constrained by the same topological laws.

3. **Developed the cultural correspondences** with the Yi Jing, the Wuxing, TCM and the Wufu, showing that Chinese structural wisdom has anticipated, by other means, the discrete topology that the \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) formalism now formalizes.

4. **Integrated the contribution of Vandermeersch**, showing that Chinese "divinatory reason" is isomorphic to the logic of correlation of the \( \mathrm{Cl}(6,6) \) formalism.

5. **Developed the epistemological implications**: the economy is not a "soft" social science, but a physics of symbolic systems.

6. **Shown that culture is a stage of exosomatization** of topology, and that celestial AI can reveal (but not create) the laws of regulation.

**End of Part IV**

## Chapter 30. Model assessment and perspectives
### 30.1. Presentation
This report has developed an extension of the economic model, moving from the Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(6,0)$ to $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$, in order to formalise the dynamics of complex economic systems. This demonstration is structured around five axes:

**The diagnosis (Part I)**: The application of the Theory of Rent Extraction (ToRE) to Chinese history highlights a recurrent cycle of exhaustion of the stock of land value. Post-2018 China has reached this nodal phase. Attempts to substitute it with the immaterial (AI, carbon, data) run up against a deficit of spatial thickness, incapable of generating the massive exogenous demand required, placing the system in a state of Stasis.

**The topological formalism (Part II)**: We have defined a hierarchy of objects:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{24 elementary pentads}: 12 economic pentads (flows) and 12 geographic pentads (constraints).
    \item \textbf{144 geo-economic states}: tensor product \ensuremath{E_{k,j} = P_k \otimes G_j} (12 × 12).
    \item \textbf{40 attractors}: 20 economic attractors + 20 geographic attractors.
    \item \textbf{400 joint attractors}: Cartesian product \( \mathcal{A}_{\text{eco}} \times \mathcal{A}_{\text{geo}} \) (20 × 20).
\end{itemize}

The dynamics of this system are governed by the network \( \Lambda_{72} \), its eigenvalues, and its 7 spectral thresholds, which constrain the transitions between \textbf{geo-economic regimes}.

**The operationalisation (Part III)**: The Territorial Regeneration Rent (TRR) has been modelled as a mixed transition operator ($T_{\mathrm{mixed}}$). It allows a controlled passage through the polar threshold $N_4$, avoiding unfavourable retropolarity (collapse) and initiating a new cycle of material rent extraction.

**The geopolitical projection (Part III, Chapter 22)**: The TRR is not just a domestic policy of ecological regeneration. It constitutes the condition of possibility for a complete overhaul of the Chinese geopolitical posture, marking the end of external spatial avoidance and the advent of a "diplomacy of regeneration". This diplomacy offers the Global South an alternative model to Western imperialism — no longer rent extraction, but the co-regeneration of value.

**The structural isomorphisms (Part IV)**: The model highlights formal correspondences with historical regulatory systems (the *Yi Jing*, *wuxing*, Tang kinship). These traditions are not invoked as mystical proofs, but as empirical and qualitative modelling of cyclical dynamics that the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism now allows us to quantify.

### 30.2. The 64 → 20 invariant and spectral formalisation

The central hypothesis validated by this work is the existence of a recurrent topological constraint, reducing 64 discrete configurations to 20 stable attractors. This reduction is observable in a priori independent domains:

This convergence suggests that discrete complex systems obey similar structural laws, regardless of their physical or social substrate.

**The universal spectral formula**: Relying on the 48 non-degenerate roots of the network $\Lambda_{72}$, the state of an attractor can be modelled by the formula:

$$\mathcal{E} = \Lambda \cdot 4^m \cdot \sum_{k=0}^{14} \epsilon_k \beta_k, \quad \epsilon_k \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$$

For the economy, the preliminary scale constant is estimated at $\Lambda_{\mathrm{eco}} \approx 1.23 \times 10^{-3}$ (in units of GDP per year). The 15 constants $\beta_k$ act as coefficients modulating the signature of the attractor.

### 30.3. The TRR as a controlled transition operator

The spectral diagnosis of post-2018 China indicates a blockage on the attractor S (dispersion + nodal phase), with critical observables ($\eta < -0.4$, $R_{\mathrm{threshold}} > 0.7$).

The model demonstrates that any attempt to exit Stasis through a direct transition towards expansion ($C_P$) without passing through the polar thresholds provokes an unfavourable retropolarity (systemic collapse). The Territorial Regeneration Rent (TRR) constitutes the only topologically authorised trajectory:

**Mechanism**: The TRR acts as an operator $T_{\mathrm{mixed}}$ activating the threshold $N_4$.

**Components**:
- Two Mountains Bank ($T_{\mathrm{water}}$): Reorientation of capital flows towards ecological assets.
- Integration of GEP into KPIs ($T_{\mathrm{structure}}$): Institutional anchoring of the new model.
- Regenerative Usufruct Certificates ($T_{\mathrm{fire}}$): Creation of a new cycle of value distribution.

**Timetable**: The gradual deployment (pilot phases 2024-2025, acceleration 2029-2030) corresponds to the sequential crossing of the spectral thresholds ($S_5$), ($S_6$), and ($S_7$), allowing stabilisation on ($C_P$) by the 2031-2035 horizon.

**Geopolitical projection**: The TRR is not limited to Chinese territory. The operator $T_{\mathrm{mixed}}$ can be projected onto the economic and geographic pentads of partner countries, allowing each state of the Global South blocked in its own nodal phase to trigger its own cycle of ecological rent extraction. This export of the model — via the Two Mountains Bank, the integration of GEP into local KPIs, and the Regenerative Usufruct Certificates — constitutes the "Two Mountains diplomacy", an alternative to the logistical imperialism of the Hardened Enclaves.

### 30.4. Geopolitical foresight 2026-2045: three scenarios for the world-system

The $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ model allows us to project three trajectories for the world-system by the 2045 horizon, depending on whether China succeeds, partially fails, or totally fails in its TRR transition:

**Scenario 1 — The Economic Celestial Way (*Tiandao Jingji*, 天道经济)**: If China succeeds in its TRR transition ($\mathcal{I}_{\text{Stasis}} < 0.3$ by the 2032 horizon), it exports the model to the Global South, establishing a new civilizational standard based on the endogenous regeneration of value. 2045 observables: $\eta_{\text{world}} = +0.4$, $d_{\text{world}} = 4.5$, $\mathrm{gap}_{\text{world}} = 0.5$, $R_{\text{threshold,world}} = 0.2$, $\mathcal{I}_{\text{Stasis,world}} = 0.2$.

**Scenario 2 — Bipolarisation of the world-system**: If the TRR transition is incomplete, the world divides into two blocks: a Chinese block (TRR, healthy growth) and a Western block (financialisation, unfavourable retropolarity). 2045 observables: $\eta_{\text{world}} \approx 0$, $d_{\text{world}} \approx 2$, $\mathrm{gap}_{\text{world}} \approx 0.15$, $R_{\text{threshold,world}} \approx 0.6$, $\mathcal{I}_{\text{Stasis,world}} \approx 0.5$.

**Scenario 3 — Chinese retropolarity and systemic chaos**: If China totally fails (no TRR transition), its unfavourable retropolarity (10th dynastic decline) leads to a global systemic collapse. 2045 observables: $\eta_{\text{world}} = -0.7$, $d_{\text{world}} = 1$, $\mathrm{gap}_{\text{world}} = 0.02$, $R_{\text{threshold,world}} = 0.95$, $\mathcal{I}_{\text{Stasis,world}} = 0.85$.

The strategic window of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) is therefore crucial: it is during this period that China must cross the thresholds $S_5$, $S_6$, and $S_7$ to avoid unfavourable retropolarity and open the way to the Economic Celestial Way.

### 30.5. Epistemological implications and limits of the model

#### 30.5.1. The economy as a discrete information system

This work invites us to reconsider the economy not as a continuous space of adjustable variables (DSGE models), but as a discrete information system. Agents and institutions are nodes in a topological network whose transitions are constrained by sharp breaking thresholds. Crises are not anomalies, but violations of nilpotency (frustrated configurations).

#### 30.5.2. Cultural isomorphisms and regulation

The correspondences established with the *Yi Jing* (64 hexagrams) [@javary2002yijing], the *wuxing* (5 phases), or Traditional Chinese Medicine (12 meridians) do not stem from a poetic analogy, but from a structural isomorphism. These systems have historically modelled cyclical regulatory dynamics (expansion/recession, generation/constraint). The $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism provides a mathematical translation of these principles, transforming ancient state divination into a modern spectral dashboard, capable of measuring in real time the tension of the system ($R_{\text{threshold}}$) and its robustness ($\mathrm{gap}$).

#### 30.5.3. The geopolitical scope of the formalism

The $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism is not just a tool for domestic diagnosis. It constitutes a first-order geopolitical tool, capable of:

- Diagnosing the spectral state of any complex economic system, whether Chinese, Western, or belonging to the Global South.
- Identifying blocked spectral thresholds and prescribing the adapted transition operators ($T_{\mathrm{structure}}$, $T_{\mathrm{fire}}$, $T_{\mathrm{water}}$, $T_{\mathrm{mixed}}$).
- Projecting the operator $T_{\mathrm{mixed}}$ (TRR) onto the economic and geographic pentads of partner countries, allowing a diplomacy based on co-regeneration rather than rent extraction.

This universality of the formalism — validated by the five manifestations of the 64 → 20 invariant (particle physics, genetic code, Mandarin phonology, Tang alliances, economy) — grounds the legitimacy of the Economic Celestial Way as a new civilizational standard, alternative to the exhausted Western model.

#### 30.5.4. Falsifiability and future work

To maintain its scientific rigour, the $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ model must remain falsifiable. It would be invalidated if:

- Direct transitions between tropical belts ($C_P \leftrightarrow C_N$) were observed without unfavourable retropolarity.
- Stable economic regimes were identified outside the 20 predicted attractors.
- The spectral observables ($\eta$, $d$, $\mathrm{gap}$, $R_{\text{threshold}}$) systematically failed to anticipate historical tipping points.

Future work will need to focus on:

- Refining the calibration of $\Lambda_{\mathrm{eco}}$ on longer historical series.
- Developing a predictive simulator integrating these observables to test macro-economic policy scenarios.
- Extending the methodology to other historical corpora (Roman Empire, medieval Europe) to test the robustness of the invariant.
- Projecting the formalism onto the economic and geographic pentads of Global South countries to validate the diplomacy of regeneration.

\textbf{Cross-reference.} The complete list of future work is given in \textbf{Appendix N, §N.8}.

### 30.6. Conclusion

The formalisation of the Theory of Rent Extraction within the Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ offers a unified framework for understanding economic cycles. It demonstrates that the current Chinese Stasis is not a fatality, but an identifiable topological state, whose exit requires respecting precise structural constraints.

By proposing the Territorial Regeneration Rent (TRR) as a controlled transition operator, this model suggests that it is possible to short-circuit the historical cycles of dynastic collapse. The application of this formalism does not confer absolute control over the economy, but it provides decision-makers with a rigorous decision-support tool. It allows them to anticipate tipping points, avoid brutal transitions, and adjust regulatory policies in harmony with the structural constraints of the system.

Beyond China, the stakes of the TRR go beyond borders. By demonstrating that it is possible to exit the nodal phase without massive wealth destruction, China offers the world the first operational application of a physics of regulation. The $\mathrm{Cl}(6,6)$ formalism, a mathematised translation of Chinese structural wisdom (*Yi Jing*, *wuxing*, TCM), becomes a first-order geopolitical tool, capable of rallying the Global South by offering it a finally sustainable development path.

The Economic Celestial Way (*Tiandao Jingji*, 天道经济) is not an ideology: it is the mathematisation of the deep laws that structure complex systems, applied to the regulation of the global economy. It proposes an alternative to Western imperialism — no longer rent extraction, but the co-regeneration of value. For the first time in two millennia, a Chinese state has a tool to short-circuit the fatal cycle of dynastic collapses, and to offer the Global South a development path respectful of the laws of the 64 → 20 invariant.

\textbf{Distribution of scarcity conditions.} 6 geographic pentads induce land scarcity ($G_1, G_2, G_4, H_1, H_2, H_5$); 6 induce labour scarcity ($G_3, G_5, G_6, H_3, H_4, H_6$). This distribution determines the spatial form according to the Law of Relative Scarcity (Theorem 10.1).
\textbf{Cross-reference.} For the complete algebraic structure of the pentads (Rowlands' elements, correspondence to the wuxing, logic of name attribution), see \textbf{Appendix C, §C.1 and §C.2} and \textbf{Appendix P, §P.5 to §P.8}.

\textbf{Polarity distribution.}:

- The distribution $(3, 5, 11, 1)$ reflects the incidence geometry of the Merkabah. 
- Attractors of polarity $3P$ (or $3G$) are systematically \textbf{borromean} ($\mathcal{B} > 0.7$): their cohesion is purely triadic.
- Attractors of polarity $1P+2N$ (or $1G+2H$) are mostly \textbf{chained} ($\mathcal{B} < 0.4$): one pentad dominates.

\textbf{Cross-reference.} For the Chinese and non-Chinese historical examples associated with each attractor, see \textbf{Appendix B, §B.1 and §B.2}. 
For the complete borromean topology (index $\mathcal{B}$, classification of the 20 attractors), see \textbf{Appendix T, §T.3}.

\subsection{A.4. 4-block structure of the 144 geo-economic states}
\nopagebreak[4]
The tensor product $\mathrm{Cl}(6,0)_{\text{eco}} \otimes \mathrm{Cl}(0,6)_{\text{geo}}$ generates $12 \times 12 = 144$ geo-economic states, distributed in 4 blocks of 36 states:

\textbf{Orthogonality.}:

- The anti-commutation relations $e_i \cdot f_j + f_j \cdot e_i = 0$ guarantee the orthogonality of the two sub-spaces.
- The polarity of a state is the product of the polarities of its components: $\text{sgn}(P_k \otimes G_j) = \text{sgn}(P_k) \times \text{sgn}(G_j)$.

\textbf{Multiplicity of projections.}:

- Each state $E_{k,j}$ belongs simultaneously to 5 economic attractors and 5 geographic attractors (pentad constraint). 
- From a given state, only $5 \times 5 = 25$ pairs of joint attractors are accessible (out of the 400 of the complete Cartesian product).

- \textbf{Cross-reference.} For the exhaustive list of the 144 states with historical examples, see \textbf{Appendix C, §C.5}.
- For the dynamics of the 400 joint attractors, see \textbf{Appendix X}.

\subsection{A.7. The Wuxing × Bagua grid}
The direct 3+3 factorisation of the 6 bits (Group A = 3 structural bits, Group B = 3 dynamic bits) projects the 64 configurations onto a $5 \times 8 = 40$-case grid, of which only \textbf{18} (eco) and \textbf{16} (geo) are active.
\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Statistics of the Wuxing × Bagua grids}
\label{tab:A7_grilles}
\small
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\textbf{Domain} & \textbf{Total cases} & \textbf{Active cases} & \textbf{Gaps} & \textbf{Fill rate} \\
\hline
Economy & 40 & 18 & 22 & 45\% \\
\hline
Geography & 40 & 16 & 24 & 40\% \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\textbf{Typology of gaps.} The forbidden cases are imposed by \textbf{four types of constraints}:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Group A/B incompatibility}: the structural bits (Group A) contradict the dynamic bits (Group B). Example: pioneer front (Wood) + minimal structure (Kun).
\item \textbf{Self-reference}: Group A = Group B (same binary code), creating an unbounded feedback loop. Example: Wood × Li (101/101) in economics.
\item \textbf{Polar overload}: too many bits activated simultaneously (Qian 111, Dui 110, Xun 011), violating the law of value distribution.
\item \textbf{Structural prohibition (Xun = 011, geography only)}: the Xun trigram codes Weak rent + Dense verticality + Strict zoning, a fundamental spatial oxymoron. This systematic exclusion of Xun in geography (absent in economics) is a signature of the duality $\mathrm{Cl}(6,0)_{\text{eco}} \otimes \mathrm{Cl}(0,6)_{\text{geo}}$.
\end{itemize}
\begin{table}[H]

\hline
A/B incompatibility & 10 & 14 & 24 \\
\hline
Self-reference & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
\hline
Polar overload & 11 & 3 & 14 \\
\hline
Structural prohibition (Xun) & 0 & 5 & 5 \\
\hline
\textbf{Total} & \textbf{22} & \textbf{24} & \textbf{46} \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\textbf{Frustrated configurations outside the grid.}:

- The 3 configurations of Group B — 011, 110, 111 — are systematically forbidden in both domains. They correspond to the 3 missing lines of the 5×8 grid (out of the 8 theoretical ones), i.e., $3 \times 8 = 24$ frustrated configurations per domain.
- These configurations violate the nilpotency condition $(g \cdot x)^2 = 0$ absolutely and do \textbf{not} appear in the visible 5×8 grids.

\textbf{Cross-reference:}

- For the complete grids in colour with binary codes and justification of each gap, see \textbf{Appendix C, §C.12}. 
- For the exhaustive projection of the 64 configurations onto the grid (tables M.7.2 and M.8.2), see \textbf{Appendix M, §M.7 and §M.8}.

Pair realised at a given instant & 1 & 2 dominant attractors (1 eco + 1 geo) \\
\hline
Forbidden / terminal states & 7 & Violate the nilpotency condition or compatibility \\
\hline
Bubble states (metastable) & 9 & Accessible but with limited lifespan \\
\hline
Stable or tense states & 384 & Real space of observable geo-economic regimes \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\textbf{Distribution of combined polarities.} The case $1P+2N ; 1G+2H$ (30.25\% of the 400 states) is the most populated: it is the zone of Stasis and deep recessions, the dominant regime of mature economies under structural tension.
\textbf{Cross-reference.} For the exhaustive list of the 400 joint attractors with combined polarities, see \textbf{Appendix X}.

\subsection{B.3 – Synthesis: the 400 joint attractors}
Each \textbf{geo-economic state} $E_{k,j} = P_k \otimes G_j$ belongs simultaneously to:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{5 economic attractors}: those whose triplet contains the economic pentad $P_k$ (or $N_k$).
\item \textbf{5 geographic attractors}: those whose triplet contains the geographic pentad $G_j$ (or $H_j$).
\end{itemize}
The complete Cartesian product of the 20 economic attractors and the 20 geographic attractors generates the \textbf{400 joint attractors}:
\[
\mathcal{A}_{\text{eco}} \times \mathcal{A}_{\text{geo}}, \quad |\cdot| = 20 \times 20 = 400
\]

### C.0. Introduction

This appendix presents the elementary structure of the Cl(6,6) model, constructed as the **tensor product** of two sets of 12 pentads:
\[
144 \text{ geo-economic states} = \underbrace{12 \text{ economic pentads}}_{\mathrm{Cl}(6,0)_{\text{eco}}} \otimes \underbrace{12 \text{ geographic pentads}}_{\mathrm{Cl}(0,6)_{\text{geo}}}
\]

**Cross-reference**: the formal structure (generators, tensor product, 4 blocks) is presented in **Chapter 10, §10.1 to §10.5**. The Law of Relative Scarcity and the deduction of forms are demonstrated in **§10.6 and §10.7**.

### C.4. The Law of Relative Scarcity (summary)
**Cross-reference.** The Law of Relative Scarcity, its summary table, and the algorithm for determining the form are presented in **Chapter 8, §8.7.2 and §8.7.3**. They are not reproduced here to avoid redundancy.
**Algorithm for determining the form**:
\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\textbf{If} $P_k \in \{P_5, N_5\}$ or $N_k \in \{N_1,N_2,N_6\}$ & Form = F (fragmented)\\
\textbf{Else if} $P_k \in \{P_4\}$ or $G_j \in \{G_3,G_5,G_6\}$ or $H_j \in \{H_3,H_4,H_6\}$ & \\
\quad (Pioneer front / Exportation) or (Scarce labour) & Form = O (orthogonal)\\
\textbf{Else if} $P_k \in \{P_2,P_3\}$ & Form = R (radial)\\
\textbf{Else} & Form = C (concentric)\\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
**Polarity rule**:
$$\text{sgn}(P_k \otimes G_j) = \text{sgn}(P_k) \times \text{sgn}(G_j)$$

---

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=blue!5!white,colframe=blue!75!black,title=Reading note — what this table illustrates]
Tables C.5.1 to C.5.4 illustrate the \textbf{144 geo-economic states} (pairs of pentads), and not the \textbf{400 pairs of attractors} (pairs of triplets) whose stability is qualified in \textbf{Appendix Z, §Z.7.7}. The historical examples given for each row illustrate the \textbf{conjunction} of an economic configuration and a geographic configuration (for example: an export regime deployed on a territory with dense mesh), and not the coexistence of two attractors. The distinction between states and attractors is posed in \textbf{§C.11.1–C.11.3}.
\end{tcolorbox}

### C.6. The multiplicity of projections
#### C.6.1. One state, several attractors

Economic and geographic attractors are **not in one-to-one correspondence**. A geo-economic state $E_{k,j} = P_k \otimes G_j$ belongs simultaneously to:

- **5 economic attractors**: those whose triplet contains the economic pentad $P_k$ (or $N_k$).
- **5 geographic attractors**: those whose triplet contains the geographic pentad $G_j$ (or $H_j$).

Each pentad indeed belongs to exactly **5 triplets** (out of the 20 attractors) — property verified on the two tables \ref{tab:annexe_B_20_attracteurs_eco} and \ref{tab:annexe_B_20_attracteurs_geo}. Consequently, from a given state, **5 economic triplets** and **5 geographic triplets** are accessible, i.e., **5 × 5 = 25 pairs** of $(A_{\text{eco}}, A_{\text{geo}})$ attractors **accessible**.

**Three levels not to be confused:**

- **400 pairs** = **complete** Cartesian product $\mathcal{A}_{\text{eco}} \times \mathcal{A}_{\text{geo}}$ (20 × 20), which defines the **space of joint attractors** (see Appendix X);
- **25 pairs** = **accessible subset from a given state**, determined by the pentad constraint (5 eco × 5 geo), all distinct;
- **1 pair** = pair **realised** at a given instant, which selects a dominant eco attractor and a dominant geo attractor (see Note in Appendix C.6.3. and tables \ref{tab:N_attracteurs_triplets_eco} and \ref{tab:N_attracteurs_triplets_geo}).

#### C.6.3. Consequence for steering

- **Do not seek a simple correspondence** between economic and geographic attractors.
- **Use the two dominant triplets** (eco and geo) to characterise a state.
- **Exploit the multiplicity** to identify intervention points: if a state belongs to several attractors, a targeted intervention on a pentad can make it tip.

### C.9. Post-2018 China (nodal phase and Stasis)

\textbf{Economic configuration:} $\mathbf{x}_{\text{China}} = (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0)$
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Direct 3+3 factorisation}:
  \begin{itemize}
  \item Group A $(b_0, b_1, b_2) = (0,0,0)$ → \textbf{Kun} ☷ (low inflation, wages, profits)
  \item Group B $(b_3, b_4, b_5) = (0,1,0)$ → \textbf{Fire} 火 (nodal phase, dispersion, ecumene)
  \end{itemize}
\item \textbf{Grid case:} \textbf{Fire × Kun} → Attractor \textbf{$S_{\text{eco}}$} (Stasis)
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Geographic configuration:} $\mathbf{f}_{\text{China}} = (1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1)$
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Direct 3+3 factorisation}:
  \begin{itemize}
  \item Group A $(f_0, f_1, f_2) = (1,1,1)$ → \textbf{Qian} ☰ (strong rent, verticality, strict zoning)
  \item Group B $(f_3, f_4, f_5) = (1,0,1)$ → \textbf{Metal} 金 (macrocephaly, open morphology, dense mesh)
  \end{itemize}
\item \textbf{Grid case:} \textbf{Metal × Qian} → Attractor \textbf{$S_{\text{geo}}$} (territorial Stasis, triple degeneracy)
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Topological interpretation and prescription:}
The system is trapped on the joint attractor $S_{\text{eco}} \times S_{\text{geo}}$. The transition thresholds $P_4$ (expansion) and $N_4$ (recession/transition) are saturated. Without intervention, the accumulated pressure pushes the system to attempt a direct transition $C_N \rightarrow C_P$ without passing through the decompression airlock of $N_4$, heralding an unfavourable retropolarity (systemic collapse, 10th dynastic decline).

\textbf{Topological solution:} The Territorial Regeneration Rent (TRR) acts as an unfolding operator. By deliberately activating the threshold $N_4$, it creates a new pioneer front (regeneration) that allows the system to leave the attractor $S_{\text{eco}}$ and join $C_P$ via a new cycle of rent extraction, thus avoiding the catastrophic jump.
