### Z.5. Topological derivation of borromean cohesion

#### Z.5.1. The principle of borromean cohesion

The borromean cohesion $\mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}}(A,B)$ measures the topological stability of a pair of attractors. It is defined by analogy with the borromean link in topology: three rings interlaced such that none can be separated from the other two. The fundamental property is that $\mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}} \in [0,1]$. A value of 1 corresponds to a maximal cohesion (hyperstable), a value of 0 to a null cohesion (forbidden).

#### Z.5.2. The three factors of cohesion

| Factor | Term | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Combined polarity | $\mathcal{B}_0$ | Base potential (structural) |
| Topological distance | $-\alpha \cdot d_{\text{topo}}$ | Friction (reduction) |
| Hierarchical position | $+\beta \cdot \text{bonus}$ | Modulation (reinforcement) |

#### Z.5.3. The base potential $\mathcal{B}_0$ (exact definition)

\textbf{Important note.} The table below is an \textbf{approximation by polarity class} (16 classes). The \textbf{exact definition} of $\mathcal{B}_0$ (T.2.3) is:

$$\mathcal{B}_0(A,B) = \mathcal{H}(A,B) \cdot \mathcal{B}_{\text{ext}}(T_A, T_B)$$

where $\mathcal{H}$ is the harmonic mean of the $\mathcal{B}_{\text{int}}$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\text{ext}}$ is the extrinsic compatibility (table T.2.4.3). The exact values of $\mathcal{B}_0$ (calculated by `Z14`) differ slightly from the values of the table by class. The \textbf{reference values} are those of the catalogue `B_joint_400_couples_v5.csv`.

\textbf{Table by class} (approximation):

| Eco \ Geo | 3G | 2G+1H | 1G+2H | 3H |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3P | 0.75 | 0.60 | 0.40 | 0.05 |
| 2P+1N | 0.60 | 0.55 | 0.35 | 0.15 |
| 1P+2N | 0.40 | 0.35 | 0.30 | 0.25 |
| 3N | 0.05 | 0.15 | 0.25 | 0.65 |

#### Z.5.4. The topological friction

The topological friction is proportional to the distance on the hierarchical graph:

$$\text{friction}(A,B) = \alpha \cdot d_{\text{topo}}(A,B)$$

with $\alpha = 0.03$. This value was calibrated so that the maximal friction (distance 6) is 0.18, which corresponds to a moderate reduction of cohesion.

#### Z.5.5. The hierarchical modulation

The hierarchical modulation is a bonus which reinforces the cohesion when the attractors are close in the hierarchy:

$$\text{bonus}(A,B) = \beta_1 \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\text{same level}} + \beta_2 \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\text{same community}}$$

with $\beta_1 = 0.08$ and $\beta_2 = 0.05$.

#### Z.5.6. General formula (cross-reference)

The general formula of borromean cohesion is defined \textbf{once only} in \textbf{T.3.5}. It is written:

$$\mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}}(A,B) = \mathcal{B}_0(A,B) - \alpha\, d_{\text{topo}}(A,B) + \beta_1\, \mathbb{1}_{\text{same level}} + \beta_2\, \mathbb{1}_{\text{same community}}$$

The coefficients $\alpha, \beta_1, \beta_2$ are calibrated in Z.5.4--Z.5.5. The present appendix \textbf{applies} this formula (Z.7); it does not redefine it.

| 2 | ~80 |
| 3 | ~70 |
| 4 | ~60 |
| 5 | ~50 |
| 6 | ~40 |

#### Z.7.5. Method of calculation

For each pair $(A_{\text{eco}}, A_{\text{geo}})$:

$$\mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}} = \mathcal{B}_0 - \alpha \cdot d_{\text{topo}} + \beta_1 \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\text{same level}} + \beta_2 \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\text{same community}}$$

$$\mathcal{F} = \max\!\big(\mathcal{F}(A_{\text{eco}}), \mathcal{F}(A_{\text{geo}})\big)$$

$$\mathcal{S} = \mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}} \cdot (1 - \mathcal{F})$$

With $\alpha = 0.03$, $\beta_1 = 0.08$ (same level), $\beta_2 = 0.05$ (same community).

Standard qualification: \textbf{Viable} ($\mathcal{S} > 0.15$), \textbf{Fragile} ($0.05 < \mathcal{S} \leq 0.15$), \textbf{Ephemeral} ($\mathcal{S} \leq 0.05$).

Particular cases (Appendix X): \textbf{Forbidden} (6 pairs), \textbf{Terminal} (1 pair), \textbf{Bubble} (9 pairs).

#### Z.7.6. Reading note of the catalogue

The values of $\mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}}$ presented in the tables below are calculated by the general formula of T.3.5 (with topological friction and hierarchical modulation). The columns $\mathcal{B}_{\text{int}}$, $\mathcal{H}$, and $\mathcal{B}_{\text{ext}}$ are provided \textbf{for diagnostic purposes}: they allow reconstructing the base potential $\mathcal{B}_0 = \mathcal{H} \cdot \mathcal{B}_{\text{ext}}$, but do not constitute the final value of $\mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}}$.

The values of the particular cases (6 forbidden, 1 terminal, 9 bubbles) are given in Z.6. The values of the 5 remarkable cases (Stasis, bubble, optimum, alternative optimum, collapse) are given in T.4.2.

#### Z.8.2. The hyperstable classes

The hyperstable classes are $3P \times 3G$ (0.697) and $3N \times 3H$ (0.632). They correspond to the pairs $(A_{\text{eco}}, A_{\text{geo}})$, $(B_{\text{eco}}, B_{\text{geo}})$, $(C_{\text{eco}}, C_{\text{geo}})$, and $(T_{\text{eco}}, T_{\text{geo}})$.

#### Z.8.3. The stable classes

The stable classes are $2P+1N \times 3G$ (0.434) and $3P \times 2G+1H$ (0.408).

#### Z.8.4. The metastable classes

The dominant metastable class is $1P+2N \times 2G+1H$ (0.130). It contains 55 pairs.

#### Z.8.5. The frustrated classes

The frustrated classes are $3P \times 1G+2H$ (0.093) and $1P+2N \times 3H$ (0.050).

#### Z.8.6. The forbidden classes

The forbidden classes are $3P \times 3H$ (0.000) and $3N \times 3G$ (0.000). They contain the 6 strictly forbidden states.

#### Z.10.1. Identification of the dominant state

Post-2018 China projects onto the attractor S (Stasis) in economics and $S_{\text{geo}}$ (territorial Stasis) in geography. The dominant state is $(S_{\text{eco}}, S_{\text{geo}})$.

#### Z.10.2. Position in the hierarchical graph

The attractor S is at level 5 (Intersections). Its position in the hierarchical graph is central, with a degree of 8.

|---|---|

#### Z.10.4. $\mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}}$ of the pair $(S_{\text{eco}}, S_{\text{geo}})$

The calculation is as follows: 

- polarity $1P+2N \times 1P+2N$ gives $\mathcal{B}_0 = \mathcal{H}(S_{\text{eco}}, S_{\text{geo}}) \times \mathcal{B}_{\text{ext}}(1P+2N, 1G+2H) = 0.294 \times 0.395 = 0.116$; 
- topological distance 0 gives null friction; 
- level bonus (same level 5) and community bonus (C4) give $+0.08 + 0.05 = +0.13$.
- The result is $\mathcal{B}_{\text{joint}} = 0.116 + 0.13 = 0.246$, classified **metastable**. 
- With $\mathcal{F} = 0.82$, the viability is $\mathcal{S} = 0.246 \times 0.18 = 0.044$, 
- i.e., **Ephemeral** (close to the 0.05 boundary).

#### Z.10.5. Implications for the TRR

China is in Stasis (metastable). The TRR must allow exiting Stasis by activating the diagonals (N, O, P), which are the tipping points of the system. The passage through the diagonals allows crossing the $N_4$ threshold and joining the expansion belt $C_P$.
